event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: The COVID-19 pandemic is referenced in Merck’s 2023 Form 10-K primarily in two contexts: (a) realised financial consequences already embedded in 2023 results—namely lower virology revenue because demand for the COVID-19 antiviral Lagevrio has fallen—and (b) forward-looking risk that sales of the product will decline further in 2024 as the pandemic wanes. Outside of this product-specific discussion, the filing also acknowledges broader biological-threat exposure through a generic reference to pandemics in the animal-health business and in a company-wide disaster scenario clause. None of the passages point to ongoing, systemic supply-chain breakdowns, labour shortages or fundamental shifts in operating models; instead, they frame pandemic impacts as tapering. Because the filing date (26 Feb 2024) is almost four years after the WHO pandemic declaration, the Time Decay Principle classifies COVID-19 as a medium-term event, capping severity scores in the mid-range. Overall, the disclosures depict a manageable but still relevant risk—material to a single drug franchise and to livestock demand—rather than a pervasive threat to the enterprise.

evidence_list.snippet: The sales increase was primarily due to growth in oncology, vaccines, hospital acute care and animal health, partially offset by declines in virology (driven by lower sales of COVID-19 medication Lagevrio ) and diabetes.

components.reason: Explicitly links a revenue headwind to COVID-19, establishing a direct realised impact.
Indicates the impact is large enough to offset growth in several other segments, implying materiality.
No numeric magnitude is provided and the effect is already balanced by other growth, moderating severity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows a concrete, company-level financial impact from COVID-19, but without quantification and partly offset, giving a moderate risk weight.

evidence_list.snippet: Given that the Company has fulfilled government purchase and supply commitments for Lagevrio , as well as the waning impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic, the Company expects sales of Lagevrio will decline in 2024.

components.reason: Forward-looking statement forecasts a pandemic-driven sales decline, signalling continuing risk.
Provides timing (2024) and causal linkage (waning pandemic), enhancing specificity.
Risk is confined to one product line rather than the whole company, lowering overall severity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Predicts imminent revenue erosion tied to diminishing pandemic needs; specific and time-bound but limited in scope, hence a mid-level score.

evidence_list.snippet: Other risks specific to animal health include epidemics and pandemics affecting livestock, government procurement and pricing practices, weather and global agribusiness economic events.

components.reason: Explicitly names pandemics as a risk factor that could hurt a business segment.
Highlights possible operational and demand disruption in the livestock market.
Generic wording with no data or probability, so impact is uncertain and partly mitigated.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Calls out pandemic exposure for animal health but only in generic terms, yielding a modest severity assessment.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition, there may be changes to the Company’s business if there is instability, disruption or destruction in a significant geographic region, regardless of cause, including war, terrorism, riot, civil insurrection or social unrest; and natural or man-made disasters, including famine, flood, fire, earthquake, storm or disease.

components.reason: Lists ‘disease’ among potential disruptive events, implicitly covering pandemics.
Highly generic, catch-all language with no direct linkage to financial metrics or probabilities.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Provides only a vague acknowledgement that disease could disrupt operations, so it contributes minimal incremental risk information.
